A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same transfer-learning research. Their text, equations, figures and complete appendices are readable. Retained Bayesian material can be matched despite substantial restructuring and new gradient-flow analyses.

before.justification: v1 reports original finite-width Langevin and gradient-descent simulations on synthetic regression tasks, CIFAR-10, MNIST and Fashion-MNIST, including appendix experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original Bayesian simulations and reports revised neural-network experiments, additional fixed-feature fine-tuning experiments and anisotropic-data regression results.

M1.justification: v1's gradient-flow formulation resets the readout and elastically constrains target hidden weights to source weights. v2's stated sequential dynamics carries pretrained fields into target training without that elastic term and introduces general-depth MLP dynamics in Appendix B. The earlier CNN extension disappears, while Bayesian elastic coupling remains in Appendices E-F.

E1.justification: The main dataset families and linear/polynomial regression tasks remain. v2 adds anisotropic inputs with a power-law spectrum and CIFAR class-pair transfer from {0,1} to {0,9}. The within-Fashion-MNIST scenario and pooled animate/inanimate CIFAR task in v1 Figures 12-13 are absent.

E2.justification: The new fixed-feature analyses explicitly evaluate an uninformative linear-probe reference, L = 1 - ν2, in v2 Figures 1, 6 and 7. v1's displayed controls primarily use uncoupled or randomly initialized neural models. The nonlinear experiments retain their no-pretraining controls; no external transfer-learning algorithm is newly benchmarked.

E3.justification: v2 adds frozen-kernel fine-tuning protocols and replaces several elastic-coupling sweeps with training trajectories. Linear-to-quadratic regression changes from D=75, P2=20 to D=100, P2=100; the He5-to-He2 experiment changes P2 from 400 to 600. The matched CIFAR class-pair experiment changes P1/P2 from 1000/50 to 10000/200. These are different evaluation settings.

E4.justification: v2 adds sensitivity analyses separating signal, noise and crosstalk contributions, examines source richness under different source-data regimes, and tests anisotropic inputs (Figures 6-10). Several earlier gradient-flow coupling sweeps, the coupling-dependent activation analysis and CNN analysis are removed or replaced. Bayesian kernel-alignment analyses remain.

E5.justification: v1 Appendix B specifies temporal averaging of linear Langevin losses and kernels after 50,000 steps; this estimation detail is omitted for the retained results in v2. The separate nonlinear Langevin averaging schedule survives in v2 Figure 11. Neither version reports independent-run uncertainty or confidence intervals; v2's 50K Monte Carlo samples describe solver particles, not repeated experimental runs.

E6.justification: v2 adds negative-transfer learning curves, source-data-dependent polynomial fine-tuning results and anisotropic-data results. Polynomial and CIFAR gradient-flow curves are replaced under changed settings, preventing direct performance-gain comparisons. Earlier CNN and within-Fashion-MNIST results disappear, whereas the Bayesian plots are largely retained and relocated.

T1.justification: Results 2-4 and Appendix C introduce data-averaged fine-tuning analyses for population, finite-source and ultra-rich pretraining, including new limiting-loss expressions. The finite-source kernel uses an explicit ansatz with unresolved coefficients. Appendix B adds history-dependent deep-network DMFT equations. The Bayesian derivations remain, while the previous CNN derivation is removed.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions shift from parallel Bayesian/gradient-flow theories emphasizing elastic coupling to a gradient-flow framework distinguishing fixed-feature fine-tuning and jointly rich learning. New central claims concern multilayer networks, finite-source negative transfer and harmful feature collapse under ultra-rich pretraining. Bayesian theory remains but loses its central billing.

C2.justification: v2 develops explanations involving finite-sample noise, crosstalk, representation overfitting and rank-one feature collapse. Hard-to-easy transfer failure is attributed to inherited unsuitable features rather than v1's elastic tethering mechanism. Limitations now emphasize isotropic-data assumptions and restricted quantitative applicability instead of the earlier absence of dataset averaging.

D1.justification: v2 Appendix D adds a 50K-sample Monte Carlo DMFT procedure, Gaussian-field initialization, Euler updates and kernel estimation. However, v1 Appendix B's Langevin temperature, step size and training budget, CIFAR preprocessing and class balancing, A100 hardware and approximately six-hour runtime disclosures are removed. These are documentation changes, not evidence that retained experiments used different implementations.

R1.justification: v2 adds Aminian et al.'s mean-field transfer analysis and references supporting DMFT and dataset averaging. It sharpens the distinction from Tahir et al. around finite source data and revises the Bayesian comparison with prior work. The LoRA discussion and citation disappear, while the main related-work categories remain.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, theoretical exposition and conclusion are extensively rewritten. The main text is reorganized around fine-tuning regimes, Bayesian material moves to later appendices, and a DMFT primer and solver explanation are added. Terminology and source/target richness notation are also revised throughout.

P2.justification: The main figures are substantially redesigned: new fine-tuning grids lead the results, polynomial comparisons are grouped into Figure 3, and CIFAR coupling sweeps become paired training trajectories. Bayesian figures move to Appendix F, new sensitivity plots appear, and several old displays disappear. The conference template, typography and captions are also reformatted.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses v1's explicitly stated lack of dataset averaging through tractable linear transfer models, yielding clearer conditions for beneficial and harmful transfer. New fine-tuning experiments, deep-network equations and solver guidance substantially strengthen the paper's explanatory scope while retaining its Bayesian evidence. The finite-data kernel ansatz and loss of general experimental metadata limit completeness, but do not outweigh these analytical gains.
